title_en: Liu Guochu v. Ye Yushan — dispute over copyright infringement

full_text_en:
Liu Guochu v. Ye Yushan — Dispute over Copyright Infringement

Plaintiff: Liu Guochu, male, 52 years old, Art Designer of the Administration Office of the Geleshan Martyrs' Cemetery, Chongqing City, Sichuan Province.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Zelong and Zhang Heguang, lawyers of the Third Law Firm of Chongqing City, Sichuan Province.

Defendant: Ye Yushan, male, 55 years old, Professor of the Sichuan Fine Arts Institute.

Agent ad litem: Sun Shaowen, lawyer of the First Law Firm of Chongqing City, Sichuan Province.

Agent ad litem: Deng Zhangtao, lawyer of the Pingzheng Law Firm of Chongqing City, Sichuan Province.

Plaintiff Liu Guochu filed a lawsuit with the Chongqing Intermediate People's Court against Defendant Ye Yushan for infringement of copyright in the "Geleshan Martyrs' Group Sculpture" (hereinafter "Group Sculpture").

Plaintiff Liu Guochu alleged: 1. The enlarged version (also known as the final version) of the Geleshan Martyrs' Group Sculpture, which was co-created by Plaintiff and Defendant Ye Yushan, was exhibited by Ye Yushan in his own name; 2. The commemorative bronze medal awarded to the Geleshan Martyrs' Group Sculpture and the "Martyrs' Tomb Sand Table Model" designed and created by Plaintiff and others at the First National Urban Sculpture Design Proposal Exhibition was taken by Defendant as his own. The Defendant infringed Plaintiff's copyright. Plaintiff requested the court to order Defendant to make a public apology, eliminate the effects, and compensate for losses.

Defendant Ye Yushan argued: Defendant was commissioned by the sponsoring unit of the Geleshan Martyrs' Group Sculpture to create the first draft and the second draft of the Group Sculpture. On that basis, Defendant personally participated in and supervised the production of the enlarged version. Therefore, the copyright should belong to Defendant. The commemorative bronze medal was issued to Defendant by the First National Urban Sculpture Design Proposal Exhibition for his creation of the Group Sculpture sculpture work, and Plaintiff has no right to it.

After a public trial, the Chongqing Intermediate People's Court found the following facts:

In the summer of 1981, the Chongqing Municipal Committee of the Communist Youth League, the Chongqing Municipal Education Bureau, and the Chongqing Municipal Bureau of Culture decided to launch an activity among the Young Pioneers of the city to raise funds for the construction of the Geleshan Martyrs' Group Sculpture, and decided to commission Defendant Ye Yushan as the creator and designer. In late August 1981, the person in charge of the sponsoring unit of the Group Sculpture orally commissioned Ye Yushan, who accepted. On September 10, 1981, at a joint meeting to study the Group Sculpture, Ye Yushan expressed his willingness to design the Group Sculpture without compensation. On October 11, 1981, the sponsoring unit sent personnel to the Sichuan Fine Arts Institute to formally complete the formalities for commissioning Ye Yushan to create and design the Martyrs' Group Sculpture. On November 25, 1981, at the "Groundbreaking Ceremony of the Geleshan Martyrs' Group Sculpture" attended by representatives from various sectors in Chongqing, Ye Yushan displayed the first draft of the Group Sculpture (30 cm high), and explained the theme, concept, and creation process, which was approved by the attendees. At the same time, a martyr's tomb model made by Plaintiff Liu Guochu under the instruction of relevant leaders to illustrate the location of the Group Sculpture was also displayed. In March or April 1982, Ye Yushan, based on the first draft, created a second draft (48 cm high). Subsequently, Ye Yushan and Liu Guochu, guided by the basic form of the first and second drafts, directed the carpenter to make the armature for the enlarged version (final version) of the Group Sculpture. At that time, Liu Guochu, as a staff member of the Group Sculpture Project Office, under the guidance of Ye Yushan, participated in the clay sculpture enlargement and other works. Ye Yushan's students, Yu Zhiqiang, Guo Xuanchang, and He Liping, also carried out artistic shaping of the initial clay sculpture. During the clay sculpture enlargement process, Ye Yushan frequently visited the site to guide, refine, and modify, and adopted reasonable suggestions from relevant parties. Suggestions put forward by Liu Guochu that Ye Yushan considered consistent with his creative intent and expression techniques were also adopted. In early 1983, after the completion of the enlarged version of the Martyrs' Group Sculpture (2.12 meters high), it was segmented into over 400 pieces. Ye Yushan and others then enlarged them in a 1:4 ratio to make clay sculptures, cast in plaster, and handed over to workers for 1:1 stone carving using granite. On November 27, 1986, the Group Sculpture was officially unveiled.

Prior to this, in May 1984, the First National Urban Sculpture Design Proposal Exhibition was held in Beijing. Chongqing selected and submitted a reduced version of the enlarged Group Sculpture created by Ye Yushan. The "Martyrs' Tomb Sand Table Model" designed and made by Liu Guochu and others was also exhibited. After the exhibition, the Group Sculpture created by Ye Yushan received a commemorative bronze medal. The "Martyrs' Tomb Sand Table Model" made by Liu Guochu was not within the scope of the selection, and no commemorative bronze medal was issued. During the trial of this case, Liu Guochu amended his second claim: When the "Martyrs' Tomb Sand Table Model" jointly made by Plaintiff and others was exhibited in Beijing, the label indicated: Designer: Bai Zuomin; Maker: Liu Guochu. That the designer did not identify Liu Guochu as a co-designer was attributable to Ye Yushan, and Plaintiff requested that Ye Yushan be held liable for infringing on the right of attribution regarding the sand table model. Ye Yushan argued that he had no knowledge of how the sand table model was attributed at the exhibition and had no dispute over the right of attribution.

The Chongqing Intermediate People's Court held that the Group Sculpture in dispute was created by Defendant Ye Yushan commissioned by the sponsoring unit and was completed under the participation and guidance of Ye Yushan. Pursuant to Article 94 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, its copyright belongs to Ye Yushan. Plaintiff Liu Guochu made some suggestions during the creation of the Group Sculpture and performed some specific work based on Ye Yushan's drafts. This cannot be deemed as making him a co-creator of the Group Sculpture. Regarding the commemorative bronze medal, the First National Urban Sculpture Exhibition only evaluated urban sculpture design proposals; the sand table model only served to illustrate the environmental effect and attachments, and was not within the scope of evaluation. The commemorative bronze medal awarded to the Group Sculpture as a sculpture work should be enjoyed by Ye Yushan individually. As for Liu Guochu's claim that Ye Yushan infringed on his right of attribution for the sand table model, it is unrelated to Ye Yushan and does not fall within the scope of this case. Accordingly, on June 14, 1990, the court entered judgment:

1. All of Liu Guochu's claims are dismissed;
2. The copyright in the Geleshan Martyrs' Group Sculpture and the commemorative bronze medal shall vest in Ye Yushan.

After the first instance judgment, Plaintiff Liu Guochu appealed to the Sichuan High People's Court. Grounds for appeal: 1. The right of attribution for a work cannot be determined solely on the basis of a "commission letter"; in fact, Defendant Ye Yushan did not have a "commission letter" either, but only a letter of introduction; 2. There was a de facto agreed relationship between Plaintiff and Ye Yushan in the cooperative creation of the Group Sculpture, where Defendant created the first draft and Plaintiff created the Martyrs' Tomb Sand Table Model, and the two combined to form a complete design proposal.

The Sichuan High People's Court found upon trial: The Group Sculpture was commissioned by the sponsoring unit from Appellee Ye Yushan for design and creation. Ye Yushan independently created the first draft of the Group Sculpture, and the copyright in this work should belong to Ye Yushan. Appellant Liu Guochu argued that the "Martyrs' Tomb Sand Table Model" he made, combined with the first draft of the Group Sculpture, constituted a complete design proposal, and therefore there was a cooperative division of labor in the creation and design of the Group Sculpture. This argument lacks factual basis and cannot be sustained. The enlarged version of the Group Sculpture was completed under the personal participation and guidance of Ye Yushan. Liu Guochu participated in the enlargement process, performed some work, and made suggestions through oral comments or actual sculpting, but whether they were ultimately adopted and approved depended on Ye Yushan. The enlarged version of the Group Sculpture, compared with the first draft, is consistent in theme, overall structure, basic form, and expression techniques, with no substantive changes. Any variations that occurred were completed under the guidance, participation, and approval of Ye Yushan, representing modifications and improvements on the basis of the first draft. There is no fact that the sponsoring unit commissioned Liu Guochu to participate in the creation of the Group Sculpture. Nor was there any oral or written agreement between Liu Guochu and Ye Yushan for cooperative creation. Therefore, Liu Guochu's claim that he should enjoy copyright based on changes in the enlarged version he actually participated in compared to the first draft cannot be established, and he cannot be recognized as a co-creator of the Group Sculpture. The evaluation committee of the First National Urban Sculpture Design Proposal Exhibition only evaluated sculpture works, not sand table models. The commemorative bronze medal awarded to the Group Sculpture as a sculpture work should belong to the author, Ye Yushan. As for Liu Guochu's claim that Ye Yushan infringed on his right of attribution for the sand table model, Ye Yushan clearly stated that he had no dispute over the design attribution of the sand table model, and the subject matter of this claim also involves other creators. The court of first instance correctly held that this claim does not fall within the scope of the present case. The first instance judgment was based on clear facts, sufficient evidence, lawful trial procedures, and correct application of law. Appellant Liu Guochu's grounds for appeal are untenable. In accordance with Article 151(1)(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), on December 1, 1990, the Sichuan High People's Court rejected the appeal of Liu Guochu and affirmed the original judgment.
